docs.title: MayaClient
docs.text:
Bases: NyxClient

Nyx client living in Maya.

What Nyx sends is run on Maya's main thread, so it can use maya.cmds safely. Scripts find cmds, mel and om (maya.api.OpenMaya) in their namespace.

Serve from a background thread (start_in_thread, what start does) in an interactive Maya. In mayapy serve from the main thread with serve_forever, there is no event loop to hand work over to.

def run_on_main_thread(self, func: typing.Callable[[], typing.Any]) -> typing.Any:
    """Run a function on Maya's main thread and wait for its result.

    Args:
        func (Callable[[], Any]): function to run.

    Returns:
        Any: whatever the function returns.
    """
    if threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread():
        return func()

    import maya.utils

    return maya.utils.executeInMainThreadWithResult(func)

docs.title: serve_standalone(name=None, address=None, token=None, connect_timeout=None)
docs.text:
Serve Nyx from the main thread of a Maya without a UI, until Nyx is done with it.

For mayapy, after maya.standalone.initialize: there is no event loop to hand work to, so the requests run right on the calling thread. Returns when Nyx asks the client to shut down or the connection ends, it does not reconnect. Start it from a Launch Process node of Nyx with a command like

"$MAYAPY" -c "import maya.standalone; maya.standalone.initialize(name='python');
import nyx_bridge_maya; nyx_bridge_maya.serve_standalone();
maya.standalone.uninitialize()"

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str | None

name Nyx shows for this Maya, NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME if omitted, then derived from the process id.

None address str | tuple[str, int] | None

host:port of Nyx, see start.

None token str | None

token of the Nyx server.

None connect_timeout float | None

seconds to keep trying to reach Nyx, forever if omitted.

None Source code in src/nyx_bridge_maya/client.py 
def serve_standalone(
    name: str | None = None,
    address: str | tuple[str, int] | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
    connect_timeout: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Serve Nyx from the main thread of a Maya without a UI, until Nyx is done with it.

    For `mayapy`, after `maya.standalone.initialize`: there is no event loop to hand
    work to, so the requests run right on the calling thread. Returns when Nyx asks the
    client to shut down or the connection ends, it does not reconnect. Start it from a
    Launch Process node of Nyx with a command like

        "$MAYAPY" -c "import maya.standalone; maya.standalone.initialize(name='python');
        import nyx_bridge_maya; nyx_bridge_maya.serve_standalone();
        maya.standalone.uninitialize()"

    Args:
        name (str | None): name Nyx shows for this Maya, `NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME` if
            omitted, then derived from the process id.
        address (str | tuple[str, int] | None): `host:port` of Nyx, see `start`.
        token (str | None): token of the Nyx server.
        connect_timeout (float | None): seconds to keep trying to reach Nyx, forever if
            omitted.
    """
    MayaClient(
        name=name or os.environ.get(CLIENT_NAME_VARIABLE) or None,
        address=address,
        token=token,
        reconnect=False,
    ).serve_forever(connect_timeout)

docs.text:
Connect Maya to Nyx from a background thread, and keep trying until it works.

Where Nyx is comes from the arguments, then the environment, then the address file Nyx writes, see nyx_bridge.protocol.find_server_address. It does not matter whether Nyx is already running: the client connects once it is, and again if the connection drops.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_maya/client.py 
def start(
    address: str | tuple[str, int] | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> MayaClient:
    """Connect Maya to Nyx from a background thread, and keep trying until it works.

    Where Nyx is comes from the arguments, then the environment, then the address file
    Nyx writes, see `nyx_bridge.protocol.find_server_address`. It does not matter
    whether Nyx is already running: the client connects once it is, and again if
    the connection drops.

    Args:
        address (str | tuple[str, int] | None): `host:port` of Nyx.
        token (str | None): token of the Nyx server.
        name (str | None): name Nyx shows for this Maya. Derived from the process id
            if omitted.

    Returns:
        MayaClient: the running client. An already running one is returned as it is,
            the arguments are ignored.
    """
    global _client, _thread
    if is_running():
        return _client
    _client = MayaClient(name=name, address=address, token=token)
    _thread = _client.start_in_thread()
    return _client

docs.title: stop()
docs.text:
Disconnect from Nyx and stop the client started by start.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_maya/client.py 
def stop() -> None:
    """Disconnect from Nyx and stop the client started by `start`."""
    global _client, _thread
    client, thread = _client, _thread
    _client = _thread = None
    if client is not None:
        client.stop()
    if thread is not None and thread is not threading.current_thread():
        thread.join(timeout=5)

docs.title: NyxBridgeCommand
docs.text:
Bases: MPxCommand

Connect Maya to Nyx, disconnect it, or ask about the connection.

Python

cmds.nyxBridge(start=True) cmds.nyxBridge(start=True, address="127.0.0.1:47770", token="...", name="rig") cmds.nyxBridge(query=True, connected=True) # [True] once Nyx accepted Maya cmds.nyxBridge(query=True, running=True) cmds.nyxBridge(stop=True)

Maya hands back the result of a Python command as a list, nyx_bridge_maya. is_connected() and is_running() answer with a plain bool.

@staticmethod
def create_syntax() -> om.MSyntax:
    """Create the syntax of the command, for Maya."""
    syntax = om.MSyntax()
    syntax.enableQuery = True
    for flag in (START_FLAG, STOP_FLAG, RUNNING_FLAG, CONNECTED_FLAG):
        syntax.addFlag(*flag)
    for flag in (ADDRESS_FLAG, TOKEN_FLAG, NAME_FLAG):
        syntax.addFlag(*flag, om.MSyntax.kString)
    return syntax

Answer the query, or do what the flags say. Stopping goes before starting, so using both restarts the client.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_maya/command.py 
def doIt(self, args) -> None:
    """Answer the query, or do what the flags say. Stopping goes before starting,
    so using both restarts the client."""
    parser = om.MArgParser(self.syntax(), args)
    if parser.isQuery:
        self._answer_query(parser)
        return

    if parser.isFlagSet(STOP_FLAG[0]):
        client.stop()
    if parser.isFlagSet(START_FLAG[0]):
        client.start(
            address=self._string_flag(parser, ADDRESS_FLAG),
            token=self._string_flag(parser, TOKEN_FLAG),
            name=self._string_flag(parser, NAME_FLAG),
        )
